topics.name: Event Management Overview
topics.description: ITOM solution positioning, customer challenges, Event Management features, operator workspace, alert intelligence, dependency maps, and CSDM integration

introduction.overview: Event Management Overview covers the foundational concepts of ServiceNow Event Management within the ITOM suite. This domain focuses on understanding how Event Management addresses customer challenges in IT operations monitoring, its key features for event collection and alert generation, and integration with other ServiceNow capabilities.
introduction.keyConcepts: Event Management is a robust application that helps keep IT systems healthy by spotting problems quickly and fixing them. It collects events from different sources, figures out what's causing the issues, and converts them into alerts. These alerts are then analyzed, grouped, and acted upon to resolve issues and maintain system health. Event Management seamlessly integrates with various monitoring tools via connectors and listeners, enabling comprehensive data collection and correlation.
introduction.whyItMatters: Understanding Event Management's role in ITOM is essential for the CIS-EM exam. This domain tests your knowledge of how Event Management fits into the broader IT operations landscape, its value proposition for customers, and how it integrates with other ServiceNow applications like Alert Intelligence and CSDM.

topics.name: Architecture and Discovery
topics.description: Discovery and MID server architecture, Event Management architecture, CMDB integration, monitoring process, and MID server validation

introduction.overview: Architecture and Discovery covers the technical foundation of Event Management, including how events flow through the system, the role of MID Servers, and integration with the CMDB for CI binding and root cause analysis.
introduction.keyConcepts: The MID Server plays a central role in Event Management by polling external monitoring tools and sending event information to the ServiceNow instance. Events are stored in the em_event table and processed through rules to generate alerts. Alerts are bound to Configuration Items (CIs) for root cause analysis purposes. The architecture enables viewing alerts on dashboards, in Alert Intelligence, or from service maps.
introduction.whyItMatters: Understanding the Event Management architecture is crucial for implementing and troubleshooting event collection. This domain tests your knowledge of how events flow from monitoring tools through MID Servers to alerts, and how CMDB integration enables meaningful root cause analysis.

topics.name: Event Configuration and Use
topics.description: Event processing, event rules, filters, thresholds, operator workspace, message keys, CI binding, connectors, and scripting with regex/JavaScript/PowerShell

introduction.overview: Event Configuration and Use is the largest exam domain, covering the detailed configuration of event processing including event rules, field mappings, thresholds, CI binding, and advanced scripting capabilities.
introduction.keyConcepts: Event Field Mappings allow you to transform event data by mapping values from specific event fields to other fields. Mapping types include single field transforms, copy operations, regex-based mappings, reference table lookups, and advanced scripting. Event rules determine how events are processed, with options for ignoring events, applying transforms, accumulating thresholds, and generating alerts based on message keys. The evt_mgmt_admin role is required for most configuration tasks.
introduction.whyItMatters: This domain carries the highest exam weight because proper event configuration is essential for effective Event Management. You must understand how to configure event rules, field mappings, thresholds, and CI binding to transform raw events into actionable alerts.

topics.name: Alerts and Tasks
topics.description: Alert records, scheduled jobs, alert management rules, priority scores, incident creation, correlation rules, aggregation, and Service Operations Workspace

introduction.overview: Alerts and Tasks is the largest exam domain by weight, focusing on alert management rules, scheduled jobs, alert clustering, correlation, and automated response actions including incident creation and remediation.
introduction.keyConcepts: Alert Management Rules (sn_em_arm) determine responses to alerts such as opening incidents, running subflows, or launching remediation actions. Rules are evaluated every 11 seconds by scheduled jobs and run only on open alerts. Alert clustering using key values groups related alerts based on CI attributes like location or supplier. For enhanced performance, use subflows instead of workflows. Users with evt_mgmt_admin can create rules; evt_mgmt_operator can manually run them.
introduction.whyItMatters: Alert management is where Event Management delivers value by automating responses to IT issues. Understanding alert rules, clustering, correlation, and synchronization with alert grouping is essential for the exam and real-world implementations.

topics.name: Event Sources
topics.description: Identifying event sources, push vs pull methods, inbound actions, monitoring connectors, and Agent Client Collector Monitoring

introduction.overview: Event Sources covers the various methods for collecting events from external monitoring tools, including pull connectors, push listeners, and direct ingestion via email, SNMP, or web services.
introduction.keyConcepts: Event Management provides numerous pull connectors (SCOM, Nagios, vCenter, IBM Netcool, etc.) that poll external tools, and push connectors/listeners that receive events sent directly to the instance. Events can also arrive via email server, script, SNMP trap, or web service API. All connectors support external credential storage. The Operational Intelligence plugin (com.snc.sa.metric) is required for Azure Metrics and AWS CloudWatch Metrics connectors.
introduction.whyItMatters: Knowing which connectors are available and how to configure event sources is fundamental to Event Management implementation. The exam tests your knowledge of specific connector capabilities, supported versions, and push vs pull methods.

topics.name: Metric Intelligence
topics.description: Metric intelligence capabilities, metric sources, data pipeline, anomaly bounds and thresholds, and Service Operations integration

introduction.overview: Metric Intelligence covers the collection and analysis of metric data, including threshold monitoring, anomaly detection, and integration with Service Operations for proactive IT monitoring.
introduction.keyConcepts: Threshold monitoring generates events when metrics exceed defined bounds. The MID Web Server extension can receive metric data using key-based HMAC authentication. The API endpoint for raw metrics is /api/mid/sa/metrics. Timestamps in authentication requests must be within 15 minutes of the MID Server time. The Operational Intelligence plugin enables advanced metric connectors for Azure and AWS CloudWatch.
introduction.whyItMatters: Metric Intelligence extends Event Management beyond events to time-series data analysis. Understanding metric collection, thresholds, and the data pipeline is important for comprehensive ITOM implementations.
